justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modestly upward-drifting baseline across the three horizons. At the one-day horizon, the estimate of 91.5 is anchored closely to where the asset or indicator was trading at the time of the forecast, with only a small drift component built in. The slight upward progression from 91.5 to 91.8 at one week and 92.5 at one month reflects a gentle positive trend assumption — likely derived from recent momentum, mean-reversion tendencies away from a slightly depressed recent level, or a modest fundamental tailwind. The slope is intentionally shallow because I did not have strong conviction in a directional catalyst; rather, the drift represents a mild carry or trend continuation signal rather than a bold directional call.

The confidence interval widths widen in a roughly proportional way across horizons, which is consistent with standard diffusion-style uncertainty that grows with the square root of time. At one day, the 90% interval spans about 4.6 units, reflecting normal intraday-to-overnight volatility. By one week, it opens to roughly 8.6 units, incorporating the possibility of a macro data release, a sentiment shift, or a liquidity event within that window. At one month, the interval stretches to roughly 19 units, acknowledging that over four-plus weeks, a wide range of fundamental and technical developments could materialize. The asymmetry in the one-month interval — with the upper bound at 102 and the lower at 83 — reflects a slight positive skew, perhaps because downside tends to be cushioned by support levels while the upside has more open air.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside these stated intervals. On the downside, a sudden deterioration in macroeconomic conditions — a worse-than-expected inflation print, a credit event, or an abrupt shift in central bank communication — could easily break below the lower bound, particularly at the monthly horizon. Geopolitical shocks or liquidity crises are fat-tail events that my intervals do not fully capture because they are low-probability but high-magnitude by nature. On the upside, an unexpectedly strong earnings report, a policy pivot, or a short-squeeze dynamic could propel the level well above 102 within a month. These tail scenarios are precisely why stated 90% intervals should be understood as covering the central mass of the distribution rather than the full range of plausible outcomes, and users should treat the tails as genuinely open-ended.
